subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A weathered gothic stone gargoyle crouched on a cathedral ledge, wings spread in a rest pose, fangs bared, with moss and rain stains in the crevices.
spec.layout: Everything is carved stone: chunky, faceted, chisel-blocky shapes with bold readable proportions and no soft organic detail. A stone ledge (1.7 wide, 0.22 high, z -0.8..0.85) is the only floor contact. The gargoyle crouches on it in a predatory squat. The heavy haunches and hind feet are planted at z -0.1..0.15. The tail runs back from the hips along the ledge, then curls to the model's left (+X) and ends in a spade. The barrel chest rises forward of the hips. Massive shoulders carry long forearms that are planted on the ledge, with big clawed hands at z about 0.6. The neck rises from the chest. The oversized head thrusts forward and slightly up, with a broad snout, an open mouth with a separate upper and lower jaw, big fangs, heavy brow ridges, curled ram-like horns, bat-like pointed ears and glaring amber eyes. A pair of bat wings with bony fingers is spread up and back from the shoulders in a rest T-pose, reaching x +-0.95, with stone-slab membranes. The silhouette is a hunched triangle topped by wings and horns. Style on every part: facets and flat planes, visible chisel-edge highlights as small lighter wedge parts, cracks as thin dark parts, and weathering coloured by place. Moss and lichen sit on upward faces and in crevices, soot and rain streaks run down vertical faces below ledges and brows, and the underside and the feet are darker. A gothic ornament motif (pointed arch, trefoil or quatrefoil) repeats on the ledge front, the chest plate, the bracers and the wing membrane ribs. The model is left-right symmetric: build the L side (+X) and the R side (-X) with `for (const s of [1, -1])`. Parts may add their own finer joints (fingers, toes, wing fingers, jaw bones) under the listed joints, with names prefixed by their part (e.g. fingerL1, toeL1, wfingerL1).

parts.builds: The cathedral ledge the gargoyle crouches on, carved stone in 'ledge' with 'mortar' joints. A chunky slab (x +-0.85, z -0.8..0.85, y 0..0.22) with a stepped cornice lip along the front and sides (small stacked boxes in stoneLight with stoneHi chisel-edge wedges on top). Dentil blocks run along the front lip. A row of three pointed-arch or quatrefoil relief panels is built from small dark extrudes in stoneDark on the front face. Two corbel blocks sit under the front corners. Mortar lines appear as thin dark boxes forming block courses on the front and side faces. One iron cramp (iron) is set into the top near the back. Weathering: moss and lichen patches on the top (moss, mossDark, lichen) especially at the back corners and around the feet and hand contact points (leave the contact spots as bare stone), rain stain and soot streaks running down the front face below the gargoyle, thin crack parts. A small worn drain groove runs under the front lip. Do not build anything above y 0.25 except moss tufts and small stone chips.
parts.attaches: Top face at mount ledgeTop (y 0.22) carries the hands (handContactL/R), feet (footContactL/R) and tail. No joints: rigid static geometry on the root joint (bone hips) at its own absolute coordinates.

parts.builds: The torso and tail, in stone/stoneDark. A bulky loft/sweep body from the hipsCenter through spine1 to the chestCenter (spine2), with a barrel chest (wider, about 0.4 across), a narrower waist and a heavy pelvis block of the hips, all with faceted chisel planes. A paler belly plate (stoneLight) with horizontal rib-band relief. A chest plate with a trefoil or pointed-arch emblem built from small dark parts in stoneDark outlined in stoneHi. A dorsal ridge of overlapping triangular spine blades running from the neck base along the back to the tail root (stoneDark, with stoneHi edges). Pec and trapezius masses that blend into the shoulders (the arms part starts at the shoulder joints). A hip mass with a loincloth-like stone slab hanging between the legs is optional. The tail follows the tail1..tail4 joints along the ledge and curls to +X, tapering with small ridge fins on top, and ends in a carved spade-shaped tip (extruded diamond, stoneDark with stoneHi rim). Weathering: moss on the top of the shoulders and back, soot under the belly, cracks across the chest and tail, rain stains on the flanks.
parts.attaches: Neck begins at neckBase on spine2 (the head part builds the neck). Thighs start at hipSocketL/R and shoulders at shoulderL/R, and wing roots start at wingRootL/R, all built by other parts. The tail lies on the ledge top (ledgeTop, y 0.22, tail axis y >= 0.3). Rides hips, spine1, spine2, tail1..tail4.

parts.builds: The neck and head, the signature feature with the richest construction. The neck is a thick sweep over neck1 and neck2 with a stone mane ridge of blades. The head is a big blocky skull at headCenter (about 0.36 wide, 0.3 tall) with a broad flat snout reaching to z about 0.9 and a heavy brow ridge, so the eyes sit under it with nothing in front of them. Build a SEPARATE upper jaw and lower jaw (lower jaw on the jaw joint, hinged at jawHinge). The mouth is open slightly, with 'mouth' dark interior parts, a stone tongue slab, and upper fangs and lower tusks (stoneHi, 6-8 sided cones, large and readable) plus a row of smaller teeth. Two big amber eyes (eyeGlow with an eyePupil slit and a dark stoneShadow socket ring, glowing) sit under angry slanted brow wedges. Nostril holes on the snout tip, a cheek plate and cheekbone ridges. A pair of big curled ram-like horns (stoneDark to stoneLight tips) sweeping back and out. A pair of tall bat-like pointed ears. A chin beard of 3-5 stone icicle spikes and a chin boss. The face is carved with chisel facets, cracks, and moss on the brow top and between the horns, soot and rain stains under the eyes.
parts.attaches: Neck starts at mount neckBase (the torso chest top, spine2) and rides neck1 and neck2. The skull rides head and the lower jaw rides jaw (hinge at jawHinge). No contact with the ledge. Nothing may be placed in front of the face.

parts.builds: Both forelimbs (build L at +X and R at -X), in stone/stoneDark. A massive shoulder pauldron block with chiselled ridge plates (a stoneHi edge wedge and a spike) at shoulderL/R, an upper arm sweep to elbowL/R (with an elbow spike), a long muscular forearm to wristL/R, and a gothic bracer on each forearm: a band with a repeating pointed-arch or trefoil relief motif. Big chunky hands planted flat on the ledge at handContactL/R (x +-0.3, z about 0.62, y 0.25), each with 4 thick fingers fanned forward (digit chains, joints fingerL1.. / fingerR1.. under handL/R, 2 segments each) and a thick thumb, ending in curved claws (stoneHi, cone-shaped, gripping the ledge lip edge). Knuckle bumps. Weathering: moss in the elbow creases and on the pauldrons, rain stains on the forearms, soot on the underside.
parts.attaches: Starts at shoulderL/R on spine2 (the torso part builds the chest and trapezius up to there). Hands rest on mounts handContactL/R at ledgeTop (sink at most 1 cm). Rides shoulderL/R, elbowL/R, wristL/R, handL/R and its own finger joints.

parts.builds: Both hind legs, digitigrade and crouching (build L at +X and R at -X), in stone/stoneDark. A thick thigh haunch from hipSocketL/R to kneeL/R with a big rounded-faceted muscle block and a knee spike, a shin back to ankleL/R, an ankle spur, then a long foot to footL/R. Each foot has three forward toes (digit chains under footL/R, e.g. toeL1.., 2 segments each) plus a rear dewclaw, all with thick stoneHi claws gripping the ledge. The feet rest at footContactL/R (x +-0.34, z about 0.12, y 0.25). Thigh striations as thin dark parts, a gothic leaf-trim band at the knee. Weathering: moss on top of the thighs and toes, soot and rain stains on the shins, cracks, and darker stone at the underside.
parts.attaches: Starts at hipSocketL/R on hips (the torso part builds the pelvis). Feet rest on mounts footContactL/R at ledgeTop (sink at most 1 cm). Rides hipL/R, kneeL/R, ankleL/R, footL/R and its own toe joints.

parts.builds: Two large bat-like wings (build L at +X and R at -X), spread upward and back from wingRootL/R in a rest pose. Each wing has a thick bony arm sweep over wingShoulder -> wingElbow -> wingWrist (a stone bone with knuckle bumps and a wrist spike/thumb claw), then four long tapered finger bones (digit chains, joints wfingerL1.. / wfingerR1.. under wingWrist, 2 segments each) that fan out and down and back to wingtips (reaching x +-0.95, y >= 0.5, z down to -0.65). Stone-slab membranes ('membrane' with 'membraneEdge' trim, via b.membrane) are stretched between the fingers and body with scalloped trailing edges. Each membrane panel gets an inset gothic motif: a pointed-arch tracery rib and small trefoil cutouts as thin dark parts in stoneDark seated on the surface, plus a feather-like chisel rib pattern. Weathering: moss on the upper arm bone tops and wing root, rain stain streaks running down the membranes, cracks and chipped edges (small notches).
parts.attaches: Roots at wingRootL/R on spine2 (the torso's upper back, between the shoulder blades). Rides wingShoulderL/R, wingElbowL/R, wingWristL/R and its own finger joints. The wing must clear the head (keep |x| > 0.25 above y 0.9 for z > 0).

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the gargoyle's proportions for the ledge pose—roughly 1.1m tall crouched with a wingspan near 1.8m, settling on dimensions for the overall size.

Now I'm laying out the stone ledge dimensions and the gargoyle's pose crouched on top, facing forward with haunches back and forearms planted. I'm mapping the joint hierarchy—hips as root, spine chain up through neck to head and jaw, plus tail, shoulder/arm chains, leg chains, and wing roots with finger digits—then dividing the model into parts: body/torso with tail, head with horns and jaw details, arms with clawed hands, legs and feet, wings with membranes, and the ledge itself.

I'm working out actual coordinates for the pose: ledge top height, hip and shoulder positions, neck and head placement, and how the wings spread outward and upward from the shoulders to their peak height.

Now I'm figuring out the overall bounding box dimensions, factoring in the tail curling back over the ledge, the hands resting at the front, and the wingspan width, then starting to lay out the joint hierarchy beginning with hips and spine.

Still defining joint positions...

For fingers I'll let part builders add their own sub-joints with distinct prefixes rather than listing them all in the main spec, just defining key joints like the hand. For wings, I'm placing wingBase, wingElbow, and wingWrist joints that angle up and outward from the spine.

Now I'm working out hind leg joint positions, placing hip and knee joints with coordinates and directions to form a natural bent-leg shape.

Still defining joint hierarchy...

Now I'm settling on a stone-toned palette with mossy greens and lichen accents for weathering, plus subtly glowing amber eyes to give the gargoyle some life.

Finishing the color list with wing membrane tones, crack and soot details, and iron fittings, I'm defining attachment points for the ledge, neck, head, shoulders, hips, tail, and wings before starting to build out the actual box geometry for each part.

For the ledge, I'm shaping a floor-anchored box with plinth, cornice moulding, dentils, a quatrefoil carving, moss patches, and rain streaks, budgeting around 130 for detail. The torso box builds out the loft, belly, ribs, spine ridge, haunches, pecs, and a four-jointed tail with a spade tip, dipping low near the ledge, budgeted around 170. Now I'm starting the head box dimensions.

Continuing to the head, I'm fitting neck, skull, snout, jaws, horns, ears, brow, eyes, teeth, beard tufts, and a mane ridge into an extended bounding box since the snout overhangs the ledge, budgeted around 190 with an updated overall size. For arms I'm placing shoulders, forearms, hands, claws, and bracers at budget 150, and for legs I'm defining thighs, shins, feet, toes, claws, and knee spikes at budget 130, deciding that the torso owns the hip mass while legs take over from the hip joint. Now I'm starting the wing box dimensions.

The total part budget adds up to 900 as expected, and I'm checking the wing's z-depth against the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fingertip joint positions to confirm the bounding box fits. With the layout finalized, I'm ready to write the JSON description, incorporating faceted blocky chisel marks, place-based weathering, left-right symmetry, and a repeated gothic ornament motif (pointed arch, quatrefoil, trefoil) across the ledge, wing membranes, chest emblem, and bracers, using the convention that left is +X.

I need to name the leg joints following the naming convention, settling on prefixed names like legsToeL1 since they must start with "legs." I'm planning the joint positions for hip, knee, and ankle on each side, mirroring for left and right legs.

For geometry, I'm thinking through capsule and rod shapes to connect hip-knee-ankle-foot, adding muscle-like icosahedron blocks at the thigh for visual bulk, plus small flattened shapes for moss detailing on top.

Now I'm working out thigh striations as thin dark offset rods, spiky knee protrusions pointing forward-outward, and a ring of small spikes circling the knee joint using the joint's frame for orientation.

Continuing down the leg, I'm defining the shin as a tapered rod from knee to ankle, adding a soot-streak detail and a backward-pointing ankle spur spike, then building the foot as a tapered rod with a pad box and three toe chains fanned out using separate joint chains with two segments each to form the toe tips.

For each toe I sweep the chain with a tapered radius and add a small claw spike at the tip, positioned off the last joint. I'm also adding a rear dewclaw spike angled back-and-down near the ankle, clamped so it stays above the ledge surface, and setting the toe sweep radius so the bottom sits flush with the ground plane.

I add tiny flattened moss bits on top of toes and thin dark boxes for surface cracks, using darker stone tones for the underside of the shin. For the thigh I'm offsetting points along the hip-knee line to create outer surface strips, then running several thin rods between offset hip and knee points with slight z-shifts to form striation detail.

I'm figuring out how to type the buildArms function parameters since the Ctx type isn't directly imported, so I'll just use loose typing to avoid issues, making sure joint names start with "arms".

For added finger joints I'm resolving a naming conflict by going with armsFingerL1 style to satisfy the "start with arms" rule while keeping the part identifiable. Now I'm sketching out the overall arm geometry plan: shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand positions for each side, building pauldron armor with faceted shapes and spike details, then shaping the upper arm as a hexagonal capsule between shoulder and elbow joints.

Elbow gets a low-poly sphere with a spike cone, forearm is a tapered capsule with added muscle bulges, and I'm building bracers as short hexagonal tube sweeps with carved pointed-arch details extruded onto the outer face using a custom arch outline profile.

Placing the three arches along the forearm's bracer band, interpolating positions between wrist (0.3,0.3,0.52) and elbow (0.3,0.55,0.38), using a simple upward vector for orientation. Now I'm figuring out the hand's palm box dimensions and position, sizing it to sit with its bottom near the ground contact point at y=0.25.

Setting up the four fingers as fanned joint chains from the knuckles, computing each finger's spread offset and the three joint positions curving upward and outward, with tapering radius along the chain to keep the fingertips sinking appropriately near the surface.

Working through knuckle spheres and thumb placement now, positioning the thumb chain inward along the hand's inner edge, then sorting out unique naming for the finger segments across each of the four fingers.

I'm sketching out a box helper for geometry placement with position and optional rotation, plus weathering details like moss patches on the pauldron, soot underside, rain stains down the forearm, and thin crack lines. Now sketching the pauldron shoulder block dimensions and offset position.

Still writing the ridge plates and spike cone geometry for the pauldron, plus a small trefoil detail made from squashed spheres on the outer face. Planning to keep the code loose with `any` typing and loop over a side parameter for symmetry.

For claws I'll use the spike helper with tip direction arrays, add a forearm muscle bulge via a scaled icosahedron near the elbow, and connect joints with capsule bones using radius arrays and bone/color options.

I'm sketching the buildHead function signature, planning to use the neck1, neck2, head, and jaw joints with their positions typed loosely to keep it flexible.

Now I'm figuring out the box dimensions for the skull and snout, then sketching helpers for cones and sweeps to shape the neck and mane, with bones attached to the right joints for each piece.

For the mouth, I'm placing the lower jaw slightly dropped to suggest a subtle open-mouth look rather than animating the jaw pose, then adding a dark gap box for the mouth interior and positioning fang boxes near the upper jaw corners.

Now I'm figuring out the fang and tusk geometry — cones pointing downward for the upper fangs sitting near the snout's bottom edge, and upward-pointing tusks from the lower jaw that need their x-position widened so they clear the upper jaw and sit just outside the snout's width.

Shifting to the eyes and brow: I'm placing small amber eye spheres with dark socket rings and slit pupils on the skull's front face, adding a brow ridge box above, and angling wedge-shaped boxes on each side with a z-rotation to create an inward-sloping brow line.

Now I'm sketching out the horn curves as a swept path of points rising from the sides of the head, curling outward and up before tapering toward a downward-curling tip.

I'm deciding to skip the ridge-ring detail on the horns for simplicity, and moving on to shaping the ears as a pointed extruded triangle.

Still placing facial details...

Now adding weathering effects like moss patches, soot streaks under the eyes, and surface cracks, plus small highlight wedges along the brow edges for a chiseled look. I'm also adding mane blades along the neck bone and a stone collar, using jittered randomization helpers for natural variation, then placing moss tufts near the top of the skull based on the calculated height values.

I need to plan the wings section, using the existing shoulder joints and adding finer finger joints prefixed with the part's name, like "wfingerL1", following the established naming convention.

Now I'm working out the geometry: shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions form the wing bone, and the fingers fan outward from the wrist, spreading downward and backward with tips at varying x, y, z coordinates to create a natural wing shape within the bounding box.

I'm planning each finger as a three-point chain (wrist, mid, tip) with a slight bow, using named segments for parenting and a tapered sweep radius along each digit.

For the arm, I'll sweep a catmull curve through shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints, binding bone weights to each joint so the mesh deforms correctly, with a faceted hexagonal cross-section and tapering radius. Then I'm setting up membrane patches stretched between neighboring finger edges to form the wing surface.

Defining membrane panel edges...

I'll drop the rod idea and instead add small claw-like wedges at the fingertips, skipping the scalloped trim complexity for now. For membrane surface decorations, I'm figuring out positions by interpolating between adjacent finger points across the panel, then offsetting along the panel's normal direction to seat details on both faces of the thin membrane.

Now I'm sketching rib and arch tracery for each panel: a straight centerline rib plus a pointed-arch shape built from a curved path through several control points, lifted slightly off the surface and mirrored onto both faces, with everything rigidly attached to the wing's wrist bone for simplicity.

I'm adding a trefoil motif of three small discs arranged in a triangle near the arch apex, plus an extra disc at the center, using thin cylinders oriented along the surface normal. Tallying it up, I'm at roughly 56 parts across all panels and faces, and now I'm considering adding a couple of thin rain-streak boxes per face to finish the detailing.

I'm realizing the wing decoration count is ballooning too high—arm sweeps, knuckle spheres, claw tips, moss patches, and finger joints are adding up to around 112 parts across both wings. I'm scaling back the per-panel detail to just the arch, trefoil, and a single center rib, cutting it down to about 80 parts total, plus a couple of streak accents per panel on one face only.

Still computing panel normals...

Writing joint lookup and mirroring logic...

Adding fingertip claw spikes along the tangent direction, then placing thin rain streak rods on the membrane faces, reducing to roughly one streak per panel to keep the wing from looking too busy.

Now I'm adding a couple of thin crack-colored rods onto the arm, then tuning the body panel path points so the edge connects naturally near the arm root and finger4's wrist-to-tip span, adjusting coordinates to make the geometry line up better.

I'm checking that the finger tip stays clear of collision bounds against the torso, then bowing the finger midpoints slightly outward using a lerp offset, and setting up the panel pairing scheme between adjacent fingers and the body with smoothed membrane bones.

For naming the chains, I'm deciding to use unique identifiers like wfingerL1 through wfingerL8 for each finger segment per side, making sure each two-point chain spans properly with catmull knots, and confirming the path edges can take a bone override while otherwise following the chain.

Now I'm working out the sweep geometry for the fingers and arms—using b.sweep with tapered radius arrays and hexagonal cross-sections, tying the arm sweep to shoulder/elbow/wrist bones with a smooth radius taper, and setting up a helper function to interpolate panel positions by lerping between two path points at a given parameter.

I'm placing moss clusters along the arm's upper surface at a few points along its length, offsetting them by the radius so they sit on top rather than embedded.
